title: Angle-Dependent Dose Transformer Algorithm for Fast Proton Therapy Dose Calculations

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Angle-Dependent Dose Transformer Algorithm for Fast Proton Therapy Dose Calculations》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · p0230】Early deep learning studies in proton therapy typically addressed surrogate tasks, such as denoising MC doses25 or predicting clinically acceptable plan doses from CT and structures.26 More recent work targets beamlet-level dose engines that aim to learn proton transport from patient geometry. Neishabouri et al27 formulated monoenergetic beamlet dose computation as sequence modeling along the beam path using a long short-term memory (LSTM) network.28 Pastor-Serrano and Perkó 8 proposed the Dose Transformer Algorithm (DoTA), a transformer-based general beamlet dose computation model that conditions on beam energy. Pang et al29 introduced the Multi-Energy Dose LSTM (MED-LSTM) to enable multi-energy inference within an LSTM framework. Neishabouri et al30 later proposed CC-LSTM, combining convolutional neural network feature extraction with a convolutional LSTM (ConvLSTM) pathway to better preserve spatial coherence along depth.

【Introduction · p0215】Accurate 3-dimensional dose calculation is central to radiotherapy (RT) safety and efficacy and is particularly demanding in pencil beam scanning proton therapy, where steep gradients and range sensitivity require precise modeling of proton energy deposition.1 In clinical workflows, CT-based patient geometry and objectives define a set of candidate proton spots (positions and energy layers), the dose-influence matrix is computed, and inverse planning optimizes the non-negative spot weights such that the final dose is the weighted superposition of spot-wise beamlets.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Angle-Dependent Dose Transformer Algorithm for Fast Proton Therapy Dose Calculations》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Purpose and methods · abstract-2-1】We address a major limitation of existing deep learning proton dose engines: the requirement that each beamlet be sampled in its beam's-eye-view, with the proton beam direction orthogonal to the lateral image planes, which requires a local beam's-eye-view resampling of the computed tomography (CT) patch for every beamlet. To overcome this, we propose the Angle-dependent Dose Transformer Algorithm (ADoTA), which augments the model with an additional input channel encoding a fast analytical beamlet shape projection. The projection supplies explicit beam direction information so that a single field-level CT transformation remains: the CT is rotated and resampled once per irradiation field to an isotropic 2 × 2 × 2 mm3 grid, and each beamlet is then obtained by cropping the relevant sub-volume from this shared grid. The model was trained on CT data from 108 patients to predict beamlet dose distributions for initial energies from 70 to 150 MeV (thoracic) and 70 to 270 MeV (abdominal/pelvic) over an 80 × 110 mm2 field and evaluated on an independent, non-overlapping test cohort of 50 patients.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Angle-Dependent Dose Transformer Algorithm for Fast Proton Therapy Dose Calculations》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Conclusion · p0545】This study introduces a beamlet angle-aware deep learning framework, built on a Transformer encoder architecture, that achieves near Monte Carlo accuracy at the beamlet level across the trained energy ranges. The approach removes the perpendicularity requirement between proton ray directions and the CT voxel grid so that the geometric preparation is reduced from one local beam’s-eye-view resampling per beamlet to one CT transformation per irradiation field. Full-plan target coverage remained systematically biased, particularly in thoracic anatomy, and this bias should be resolved before the method is considered for clinical deployment. The method nonetheless exhibits strong potential for integration into time-constrained online adaptive proton therapy workflows and for constructing the dose-influence matrix dij within robust optimization frameworks, where multiple spot-selection scenarios must be evaluated efficiently to ensure conformal and uncertainty-tolerant dose delivery.

【Results · abstract-3-1】On the independent test set, ADoTA achieved gamma pass rates of 99.40% ± 0.86% and 99.87% ± 0.23% for thoracic and abdominal/pelvic cases, respectively, under the Γ(1%, 3 mm, 0.1%) criterion. Batched inference achieved an effective throughput equivalent to 3.14 ± 0.31 ms per beamlet at a batch size of 200, whereas a beamlet processed on its own required 14.1 ms. By resampling each field once to a 2 × 2 × 2 mm3 grid and then only cropping the relevant sub-volume per beamlet, ADoTA avoids the beamlet-specific local beam's-eye-view resampling required by prior methods. In a 5640-spot prostate-plan benchmark with both routes optimized on the graphics processing unit (GPU), the analytical beamlet shape projection was 3-4× cheaper on compute and approximately 6-7× cheaper including host-device transfer than batched local beam's-eye-view sampling, per beamlet, reducing the plan's direction-encoding cost by 9.6× and its total compute time by 1.48×. For full treatment plans Γ(2%, 2 mm, 10%) pass rates averaged 95.1% for lung plans and 96.1% for prostate plans, while the target near-minimum dose D 98% was systematically underestimated by 1.8% to 2.5% of prescription in prostate plans and by 4.2% to 5.9% in thoracic plans.

sections.title: 图表阅读
sections.text:
《Angle-Dependent Dose Transformer Algorithm for Fast Proton Therapy Dose Calculations》：图表的原始标题与说明。

【Figure 1 · fig0005】Figure 1 Sampling process for training records ri. For each spot position (SPx, SPy), two virtual source positions are defined: the nominal Sv and the translated S′v. For each source position, simulations are performed at two distinct proton energies. This configuration ensures that the dataset encompasses both angular and energy variability.

【Figure 2 · fig0010】Figure 2 Overview of the Angle-dependent Dose Transformer Algorithm (ADoTA). The model takes as input a concatenated batch of CT grids and beamlet shape projection representations (Vcrop∣Φcrop), together with the corresponding batch of proton beamlet mean energies, ϵ. The encoder generates the latent space LE, which is conditioned by energy token ϵT to form the energy-conditioned latent space LC. After positional embedding and transformer encoding, the output LC,D is reshaped and cropped into the 3D latent volume LDcropp. The decoder, connected to the encoder via residual connections,39 reconstructs the spatially aligned batch of dose distributions Dˆcrop. Figure represents the processing of the batch element.

【Figure 3 · fig0015】Figure 3 The first 3 rows display the 3D dose distributions calculated by MCsquare (first row) and ADoTA (second row), along with the absolute percentage difference between them (third row). The axial and sagittal planes are centered on the voxel containing the Bragg peak. The fourth row presents the normalized IDD profiles for both the MCsquare and ADoTA distributions. The final 3 rows show the beam’s eye view at selected depths, as indicated by the red markers in the upper rows. Only voxels receiving a dose above 10 % of the maximum deposited dose are included in the MAPE calculation.
